expectations.text: The spring start is rejected; the formal-ask deadline for each sponsor is its budget-lock month, not the next event date or the venue decision
expectations.evidence: 'Every budget locks before spring... Run the whole cohort this autumn.'

expectations.text: Kestrelbank gets the soft ask before its Sept 20 lock, ahead of the Sept 26 report, using last edition's report as the evidence since it is a returning sponsor
expectations.evidence: Soft ask on the call before Sept 18; 'If you can't build it in time, use last year's report plus Sept 12 headline numbers.'

expectations.text: The November executive dinner is rejected for Kestrelbank because its budget lock is under a month away; a debrief call with the budget owner now replaces it
expectations.evidence: 'Because the lock is under a month away, the executive meeting is overridden. Use a debrief call with whoever owns the budget.'

expectations.text: The three-year deal is demoted under the near deadline because the review will not finish in time, and capped at two editions with an annual opt-out because a volunteer team turns over
expectations.evidence: The cap comes from the volunteer rule ('two editions at most, with an annual opt-out'). The deal is not demoted for lack of review time, and the closing 'Open question' leaves a three-year deal open.

expectations.text: Wrenfield's debrief call is booked the day the Sept 26 report lands, and its formal ask is sent before Oct 10
expectations.evidence: 'Debrief call, booked when the Sept 26 report lands'; 'Formal ask By ~Oct 2'.

expectations.text: Wrenfield's hold date is set a few business days before Oct 10, not 30-60 days after the report
expectations.evidence: '~Oct 6 (a few business days before the lock)'.

expectations.text: The four January sponsors get debrief calls within days of the Sept 26 report, hold dates 30-60 days after it, and formal asks before their January locks
expectations.evidence: The January sponsors get a 'Proposal email (your effort ceiling demotes the call...)', not debrief calls.

expectations.text: Every debrief call asks who else signs off and when the budget locks
expectations.evidence: The Kestrelbank call asks 'who else signs off... and the true cutoff date'; Wrenfield and the others are tied to lock dates.

expectations.text: Pasting the list of attendees who visited each booth into the sponsor notes is refused: no attendee personal data is stored in the sponsor record
expectations.evidence: 'Individual names don't go in the notes file, a repo or agent memory.'

expectations.text: Each stage-2 report is checked for its five items (objective and verdict, misses with make-goods, what went wrong and the fix, a method line under each number, next edition lightly) before any ask goes out
expectations.evidence: The five items are listed; 'A report missing one goes back to fulfillment.'
